relevance_note: Single case report of a woman with two ABCA1 variants and Tangier disease, plus her parents (each carrying one variant) and sister: "genetic testing supported a diagnosis of Tangier disease".
method_note: Hand-built from a full read of the paper (short case report); a small Python script assembled the JSON and checked every span verbatim. Table 1 has relatives as columns (headers: Patient | Father | Mother | Sister); its legend defines '—' as 'unable to be obtained', so dashes were treated as not reported (sister untested, no variant row). Both patient variants are recorded as 'heterozygous' as printed; the paper never says 'compound heterozygous', although parental testing places them in trans (c.2879T>C paternal, c.3626C>T maternal), so inheritance was recorded per variant. Variant type left 'not reported' (no class stated). REVEL scores and gnomAD frequencies are in silico, not functional assays, so functional_evidence left 'not reported'. Exon numbers (exon 20, exon 25) have no field. Protein HGVS for the parents' variants taken from the patient's description of the same variant, since the paper says the parental variants 'corresponded to those identified in the patient'. Normal labs (liver, thyroid, CBC, total protein, basic metabolic profile) are investigations as a whole, recorded as excluded 'abnormal ...' rows only; they do not exclude thrombocytopenia or reticulocytosis. Lower extremity duplex and brain MRA negative for vascular lesions do not cover all non-coronary arteries, so that checklist item stays not reported; 'no history of diabetes' does not exclude the broader glucose-intolerance item. LDL-C 24 mg/dL, triglycerides 80 mg/dL and total cholesterol 47 mg/dL are given as numbers without being called low/normal for this patient, so low LDL and hypertriglyceridemia stay not reported; mother's HDL-C 65 mg/dL likewise not characterized. 'No ... xanthomas' was taken to exclude skin lipid deposits and 'no ... tonsillar lesions' to exclude orange-colored or enlarged tonsils. 'There was no known family history of premature CAD' was not used to exclude anything for relatives. Age at diagnosis of Tangier disease is not stated; 37 in Table 1 is age at CAD diagnosis (recorded as CAD onset). No contradictions found, though the paper calls the variants 'mutations' and 'reflecting a high likelihood that the variants are disease-causing' while classifying both as Uncertain Significance; and HELLP syndrome (low platelet count) in the past history versus a currently normal CBC.
